subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity & isolation — summary + next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@luminadiag.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity & isolation — summary + next steps

Hi Sara / team,

Thanks again for the time earlier today — appreciate the candid discussion about where Lumina is on model rollout. Wanted to capture the key points and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Recap of pain & goals
- Production workload: ~18–22 RPS at 2–4s p95 on current transformer models; peaks up to ~35 RPS during batch ingest windows.
- Data sensitivity: PHI in inference inputs; must remain in US-only tenancy and have customer-managed KMS.
- Isolation requirement: logical tenant isolation + dedicated GPU pool to prevent noisy-neighbor risk during clinical spikes.
- Latency SLA target: 99th percentile below 4s for single-chat queries; throughput target 30 RPS sustained.

Our proposed architecture (high level)
- Reserved Dedicated pool: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs initially (can scale to 16 based on traffic), single-tenant scheduling with KV cache pinned to pool.
- Autoscaling buckets: fast-burst allowance up to +50% for scheduled batch windows; capacity arbitration policy to favor isolation SLOs.
- Security & compliance: private VPC peering option, audit logs to send to your SIEM, integration with your KMS/HSM.

Operational & commercial asks from Lumina
1) Confirm whether you want an on-prem proxy or VPC peering for data egress controls.
2) Procurement: target budget window and PO cadence so we can size billing term (monthly vs. annual commit).
3) SLA flexibility: do you require a 99.9% uptime SLA or is 99.5% acceptable for the pilot?

Attachments: I’ve attached a short "Redwood Dedicated Options" PDF that maps sizing to estimated token costs and expected p95/p99 latencies for the two model sizes you mentioned. I also dropped a working MOP (Method of Procedure) draft into Drive for collaboration — link below.

Immediate next steps (suggested)
- Lumina: confirm preferred isolation topology (VPC peering vs on-prem proxy) and procurement contact (Procurement@luminadiag.com).
- Redwood: provide an SOW estimate and a scoped MOP for production cutover by EOD Thursday.
- Schedule a procurement walk-through next week (30–45 min) to align on billing cadence and required contract language.

If those items look right I’ll loop in Jordan (pricing/SOW) and Monica (onboarding/ops) to draft the formal mutual action plan.

Thanks — Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Account Exec, Dedicated Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated capacity & isolation — summary + next steps

Thanks Sean — this is helpful and captures our discussion well. A few clarifications from our side:

- Isolation topology: We prefer VPC peering for the pilot so that we maintain tight network controls; will need your standard diagram to share with our cloud security team.
- KMS: customer-managed keys are a hard requirement (we need envelope encryption with keys rotated in our KMS).
- SLA: for clinical-facing endpoints we need 99.9% uptime for production; pilot can run at 99.5% if we have a clear ramp schedule.

Procurement note: copying Procurement — we typically run 30–60 day PO cycles and will need a pricing sheet with line items by GPU count and a clear cancellation/scale-up clause. Also please include a data-residency addendum for US-only tenancy.

Can you also confirm whether the autoscale burst (+50%) is billed as on-demand overage or covered within a reserved-burst pool? That will affect our cost modeling.

We’re available for a procurement call next Tuesday (Mar 30) between 10–12 PT. If you can share the SOW estimate and MOP link beforehand that would be great.

Sara Chen
Head of Platform Engineering
Lumina Diagnostics
sara.chen@luminadiag.com
